A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, training algorithm, and central framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original self-improvement, solver-verifier evaluation, Pass@K, and external-data allocation experiments on Math and GSM8k, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds ProntoQA experiments and direct empirical checks of the gap-dynamics relationship.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains score filtering, length-normalized Best-of-N selection, and the uncertainty-minimizing SFT objective. Cross-improvement still substitutes external responses for selected training targets. The revised mathematical modeling assumptions do not establish a changed training algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 extends evaluation beyond Math and GSM8k mathematical problem solving to ProntoQA question answering. Appendix C.2 reports training dynamics, curve fitting, candidate-count evaluations, and cross-evaluation for this added task coverage; the original datasets remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding mathematical experiments retain the TF/QE methods, five Phi/Llama solver-verifier models, and Initial/Baseline/Early/Uniform/Late comparisons. DeepSeek-V3 already supplied external data in v1; its newly reported accuracy does not introduce another comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes the reported Uniform allocation from each of the first eight epochs to each epoch. V2 also introduces linear regression of dG/dt against G as an evaluation procedure. The retained self-improvement setup still specifies batch size 256 and ten epochs; v2 omits cross-improvement duration, so a change to that training budget cannot be established.

E4.justification: New Figures 2 and 7 directly test the assumed linear relationship between the capability gap and its rate of change across four models and both mathematical datasets. V2 also expands exponential-fit validation with separate train/test displays. Existing candidate-count sensitivity and Pass@K analyses are retained and reorganized, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report ± table entries and R² fit statistics without specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, the meaning of ±, or formal significance tests. Changed ± and R² values do not establish a changed reporting practice. The plotted model uncertainty remains a negative-log-likelihood capability metric.

E6.justification: V2 adds ProntoQA and gap-regression results and revises fitting statistics, heatmap cells, and Table 1. The Phi-4-mini Math baseline changes from 43.87% to 45.08%. Its Early/Uniform/Late values of 46.33/46.56/45.83 match v1's twelve-epoch Table 2, so they should not be treated as new gains over v1's ten-epoch Table 1; v2 leaves duration unspecified. New Figure 17(c) reports a negative accuracy gap of -0.028 for Llama-3.1-8B verifying itself on ProntoQA.

T1.justification: V1 assumes an exactly linear potential; v2 introduces a differentiable monotone function and Taylor approximation, adds self-improvement proofs, and derives initial-gap sensitivity and stopping-time corollaries. The additions contain inconsistencies: Appendix B.1 reverses the initial-gap sign, and Corollary 3.1 gives -β/(α-β), whereas its proof in B.2 gives -α/(α-β). The retained cross-improvement derivation also replaces two approximation signs with equalities in Equation (45).

C1.justification: V1's abstract promises prediction of ultimate capability using only the first few epochs; v2 instead emphasizes modeling the trajectory and quantifying limits by fitting experimental results. Early-epoch parameter estimation remains in the discussion of Corollary 3.2. The central gap-driven dynamics and external-data timing claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes low uncertainty from accuracy and identifies the framework as phenomenological rather than derived from first principles. It adds discussion of connecting α and β to model architecture. Section 5.2 drops v1's explanation that late external data require sufficient subsequent training; the existing incorrect-response and repetition limitations remain in Appendix C.2.

D1.justification: V2 omits several important disclosures: threshold σ=0.5, zero-shot prompting, neutral-score handling, evaluation subsets of 2,048/1,024 examples, and the 3,000-response external-data budget and ten-versus-twelve-epoch cross-improvement settings. Hardware and core optimizer/LoRA settings remain; N=16 and the 512-token limit are relocated into Table 2. These are substantial documentation losses, not evidence that every underlying setting changed.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works; added publication years for Amini, Chang, and Pace are metadata corrections. Section 2 and the relocated Review and Prospect discussion retain the same positioning relative to Song et al. and Huang et al.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: detailed experimental setup and evaluation discussion move into Appendix C, the main-text Pass@K subsection becomes appendix material, and the former Appendix C discussion moves to A.2. Theory is reorganized around propositions and corollaries, while cross-improvement discussion and the conclusion are condensed.

P2.justification: V2 adds a new introductory illustration, regression plots, and ProntoQA displays. The original overview and cross-improvement diagrams move to the appendix; candidate-count plots and TF/QE Pass@K panels are consolidated, and heatmaps are regrouped with reordered model axes. The separate extended-training table disappears as a display, with several results retained in the revised Table 1.

improvement.justification: ProntoQA experiments and direct gap-dynamics checks broaden empirical support, and v2 better qualifies its uncertainty proxy and phenomenological framework. However, the new proofs introduce sign and derivative inconsistencies, while settings disclosed in v1 disappear from the revised experimental reporting. These gains in validation coexist with material losses in mathematical consistency and reproducibility, preventing a reliable net judgment of overall quality.
